assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: ready

FROZEN because the AGENT lacks the behavior, not because irrlicht cannot see it. The scenario's own instruction applies: "If the agent under test cannot raise any dialog of this kind, mark the cell `agent_supports: no` and say which of the four triggers you checked." Below is each of the four, checked against `strings(1)` on both shipped kiro-cli 2.6.0 binaries — the 103 MB launcher `kiro-cli` and the 530 MB `kiro-cli-chat`, which is the REPL the row would have to exercise (`kiro-cli chat --help` reports usage as `kiro-cli-chat chat`, so the launcher is not the surface).

### Trigger 1 — a sandbox or network-access confirmation: ABSENT

`sandbox` matches 58 times in `kiro-cli-chat` and **zero** times in `kiro-cli`. Every one of the 58 is a bundled syntax-highlighting grammar or keyword list — the twig template grammar, the CSP `sandbox` directive in an HTML/CSP keyword list, a vim command list, Linden Scripting Language constants, the React HTML attribute table, a T-SQL keyword list — with exactly one exception: the prose of the `--trust-all-tools` warning, "This mode is intended for sandboxed or disposable environments only. Do not use it on a machine with access to sensitive data or production systems." kiro-cli has no sandbox to escape and no network-access gate: `network access`, `allow network` and `internet access` all match zero times in either binary.

### Trigger 2 — a first-use trust prompt for the workspace or a configured server: ABSENT AS A TURN-TIME DIALOG

There is no workspace-trust prompt — `do you trust`, `trust the files`, `trust this folder|workspace|directory|repo` all match zero times — and no per-MCP-server first-use trust prompt.

kiro-cli does have exactly one tool-less blocking dialog, and it is worth naming precisely so a future audit does not re-litigate it. The `--trust-all-tools` confirmation is a real modal: component `Rle` renders the kiro logo banner (`am`, with `agent:"kiro", mcpServers:[]`), the heading "Warning: Kiro is running in trust all tools mode", three paragraphs of risk copy, and a selector over `[{label:"No, exit"},{label:"Yes, I accept"},{label:"Yes, and don't ask again"}]`; accepting-always persists `chat.disableTrustAllConfirmation: true`. But it renders **in place of the chat UI at launch**, before any session turn exists. It is not raised by a prompt, and it produces no `working → waiting` edge — only a delayed birth. That is the same disposition codex's sibling cell gives its two startup gates (`tui/src/cwd_prompt.rs`, `tui/src/startup_hooks_review.rs`), and the row's process is explicit that the dialog must follow a `send`.

### Trigger 3 — a server-driven MCP elicitation: NOT SURFACED IN THE CHAT REPL

This is the trigger that turned codex's sibling cell to `agent=yes`, so it got the closest look. The elicitation vocabulary IS present in `kiro-cli-chat`: `elicitation/create`, `CreateElicitationRequest`, `CreateElicitationResult`, `ElicitationCapabilities` / `ElicitationFormCapabilities` / `ElicitationUrlCapabilities`, `FormElicitationParams`, `UrlElicitationParams`, `ElicitationSchema`, `ElicitationCompletionNotification`. But every one of them belongs to one of two libraries, not to the chat REPL:

- the **rmcp protocol schema** — `ClientCapabilities { roots, sampling, elicitation }` and friends are serde struct/field-name tables, i.e. type definitions compiled in with the MCP crate. A struct field named `elicitation` is not a declaration site; no construction site setting it was found.
- the **`sacp-11.0.0` ACP client library** (31 source-path hits) that backs the `kiro-cli acp` subcommand — kiro acting as an Agent Client Protocol agent for an external editor. Its handler is `case Oo.elicitation_complete: if(!t.unstable_completeElicitation) return;`, i.e. an *unstable, optional* method on the ACP client, reached over `session/elicitation/complete`.

Against that, the chat REPL's own dialogs are easy to find when they exist: the tool-permission picker's React component is present verbatim, with its option map `{allow_once:"Yes, single permission", allow_always:"Trust, always allow in this session", ...}` and its `permissionOptions`/`trustOptions` props. No comparable elicitation component exists — `setElicitation`, `pendingElicitation`, `ElicitationDialog`, `elicitationRequest` all match zero times, as do the user-facing strings such dialogs need (`needs your input`, `requires input`, `server needs`, `input needed`: zero). And enumerating every `crates/chat-cli-v2/src/**.rs` path in the binary's string table — 30 of them, including the whole `agent/acp/commands/` set — yields none mentioning elicitation, permission, or dialog. So the surface irrlicht observes has no elicitation dialog to raise.

### Trigger 4 — an auto-mode or settings review the product raises before it proceeds: ABSENT

kiro does have an autopilot mode — `this.kiroClient.setSessionConfigOption({sessionId:n, configId:"autopilot", value:"on"})`, with telemetry `chatAgentMode: AUTOPILOT|SUPERVISED` — but it is set programmatically inside session wiring, wrapped in a debug-logged try/catch, with no review dialog anywhere near it. There is nothing resembling claudecode's `auto_mode_setup_review` / `auto_mode_flagged_allow` / `managed_settings_security`. The `/settings` panels (`display`, `theme`, `terminal`, `keybindings`, `history`) are handlers invoked BY the user's slash command, never raised by the product before it proceeds. (`auto-mode` matches 16 times and all sixteen are Emacs Lisp symbol lists inside a bundled grammar — `auto-mode-alist`, `ibuffer-auto-mode`, `set-auto-mode`.)

## Why the daemon pillar is n/a rather than a verdict

With `agent=no` there is nothing to observe, so `n/a` is the honest pillar. Recording it anyway would document nothing. For whoever revisits this after the agent side changes, though, the daemon answer is already determined and is worth stating: a tool-less kiro dialog would be invisible on **both** channels irrlicht has into a kiro session.

- **No hook.** kiro-cli installs exactly two hook events, `stop` and `postToolUse` (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/kirocli/hooks.go`). `preToolUse` is deliberately not installed — the #1716 audit found it fires for every tool call with no discriminator separating "waiting for approval" from "running now". Unlike claudecode there is no `Notification` event and no matcher irrlicht could widen; kiro's own event vocabulary (`agentSpawn`, `userPromptSubmit`, `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`, `stop`) contains no interaction or elicitation event at all, so `metrics.PermissionPending` can never be set and classifier rule 0 can never fire.
- **No transcript trace.** The kiro parser recognises four envelope kinds — `Prompt`, `AssistantMessage`, `ToolResults`, `Clear` — and skips everything else (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/kirocli/parser.go`). A dialog attached to no tool call writes no `AssistantMessage` and no `toolUse`, so nothing lands in the `<uuid>.jsonl` the `FilesUnderRoot` Source tails. The parser also never sets `TranscriptPermissionPending` (copilot's signal, #1256).

Both edges the row asserts would therefore be missing, and the trailing idle would have nothing to catch: the session would read `working`, or `ready` if the tail already looked turn-done, for the whole time the modal blocked. That is no-trace-exists — `incapable`, not `bug` — and it is the verdict this cell should carry the moment the agent pillar flips.

## Driver

`ready`, and stated explicitly so this frozen verdict is not mistaken for a tooling gap. `driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/kiro-cli/driver-interactive.sh` reports `exit_clean interrupt keys reset_session restart resume rewind_fork send session sigkill slash sleep start_session wait_turn`; `DRIVE_ELICITS` (line 218) lists every one of them. A recipe for this row would need `send`, `sleep`, `keys`, `wait_turn` — all implemented. Nothing about this cell is blocked on the driver.
caveats: VACUOUS-PASS WARNING for whoever revisits this: on kiro-cli a recording of this row could not tell 'the dialog never painted' from 'the dialog painted and the daemon saw nothing' — both yield an events.jsonl with no waiting episode, and today both are the expected output. Any waiting a kiro recording DID show on this row would by construction come from something else (a stray tool-permission picker via the open_tool_stalled rung, or the waiting-cue path). Never grade this row without independent proof the modal was on screen, e.g. a tmux pane capture carrying the dialog's own text.

MAIN RESIDUAL RISK, marked assumed rather than dismissed: the trigger-3 conclusion rests on WHERE the elicitation symbols live (rmcp schema + the sacp-11.0.0 ACP client library) and on the ABSENCE of a chat-TUI component, not on driving the CLI against an elicitation-capable MCP server. This verb makes no model calls and drives no CLI, so that was not exercised. If kiro's MCP client turns out to declare `elicitation` in the capabilities it sends on `initialize` and to render a form in the REPL, the agent pillar flips to `yes` and the daemon pillar becomes `incapable` (per the body's analysis) — the route stays frozen either way, which is why this uncertainty does not change the disposition.

The one tool-less dialog kiro-cli DOES have is the --trust-all-tools confirmation, and it is deliberately not substituted here. It renders at launch in place of the chat UI, so it can only delay the birth; it is suppressed entirely on this host today (~/.kiro/settings/cli.json carries chat.disableTrustAllConfirmation: true); and the driver launches with settings.trust_all_tools=false for the permission cells, which never reaches it at all. Recording it would assert a startup gate, not the row.

Do NOT let this row collapse into tool-gate-permission-prompt (2.19) or permission-gate-non-mutating-tool (2.26). kiro's tool-permission picker — the same component for read-only and mutating tools — is what those two cells cover; this row is specifically about a dialog with no tool call in flight.

RE-ASSESS WHEN any of: kiro-cli surfaces MCP elicitation in the chat REPL (a TUI component plus an `elicitation` capability actually declared on initialize); kiro gains a sandbox or network-access confirmation; kiro moves the --trust-all-tools confirmation, or any new trust gate, to fire mid-turn rather than at launch; kiro adds an auto-mode review dialog around the existing autopilot session config; or kiro's hook event set gains a Notification-equivalent (which would also give the daemon a channel it does not have today).

recipe.notes: applicable: false (frozen). NOT a driver gap — driver-interactive.sh implements send/keys/slash/wait_turn/sleep, every step a recipe would need. kiro-cli 2.6.0 simply has no blocking dialog that belongs to no tool call and is reachable from a prompt: no sandbox or network-access confirmation, no workspace or MCP-server first-use trust prompt, no chat-REPL surface for MCP elicitation (the elicitation symbols belong to the rmcp schema and the sacp-11.0.0 ACP client library behind `kiro-cli acp`), and no auto-mode or settings review the product raises on its own. Its one tool-less dialog, the --trust-all-tools confirmation, renders at launch in place of the chat UI, so it yields a delayed birth rather than the working→waiting edge this row asserts — and it is disabled on this host anyway. Substituting the tool-permission picker is explicitly forbidden by the scenario: that behavior belongs to 2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt and 2-26 permission-gate-non-mutating-tool.
